column1: Who handles operating-system and database-engine patching for Azure SQL Database and Azure SQL Managed Instance?
column2:
Microsoft.
Microsoft patches the platform and engine for these two managed services. You still manage application schema changes and the way your application uses the database.
Review source

column1: What database-design work remains your responsibility in Azure SQL Database?
column2:
Designing application objects such as tables, indexes, and constraints.
The service operates the infrastructure, but it cannot decide what a valid customer or order looks like. Your schema defines those objects and their integrity rules.
Review source

column1: Which Azure SQL Database tier lets storage scale independently of compute for very large databases?
column2:
Hyperscale.
Hyperscale separates compute from its storage services. Storage can grow independently rather than requiring you to manage one increasingly large disk with the compute.
Review source

column1: How can Azure SQL Database Hyperscale serve more read traffic without running every read on the primary?
column2:
By adding read-only replicas.
A read-only replica can serve reports without running those queries on the primary. Keep writes on the primary and account for replica lag where it matters.
Review source

column1: Which Azure SQL Database compute tier automatically scales compute within configured limits as demand changes?
column2:
Serverless.
Serverless adjusts compute between the configured limits. That differs from manually selecting a larger provisioned size whenever demand rises.
Review source

column1: When an eligible Azure SQL Database serverless database pauses, which resource continues to incur charges?
column2:
Storage.
The data still occupies storage and must be retained while compute is paused. The pause therefore stops compute charges rather than eliminating every charge.
Review source

column1: Why can the first connection to an auto-paused Azure SQL serverless database need a retry?
column2:
Resuming the database can cause temporary connection failures.
The first connection to a paused database can start a resume and fail before it completes. A bounded retry policy lets the client connect once the database is ready.
Review source

column1: Which Azure SQL Database feature can create workload-based indexes when its CREATE_INDEX option is enabled?
column2:
Automatic tuning.
With CREATE_INDEX enabled, the service can apply a recommended index and observe its effect. That is different from forcing a previous query plan.
Review source

column1: When a query slows down after a plan change, what does Azure SQL automatic plan correction do?
column2:
It forces the last known good execution plan.
The service can force a previously better plan after a regression. The action changes how a query runs, not which tables or indexes exist.
Review source

column1: Which managed Azure SQL service offers instance features such as Agent and native cross-database queries?
column2:
Azure SQL Managed Instance.
Managed Instance provides instance features such as SQL Server Agent and cross-database queries. Confirm platform and update-policy limits for the features your migration needs.
Review source

column1: Which built-in service schedules database jobs in Azure SQL Managed Instance?
column2:
SQL Server Agent.
Create a SQL Server Agent job and schedule it to run in the instance. Azure SQL Database does not offer that same built-in Agent.
Review source

column1: What naming format references an object in another database on the same Azure SQL Managed Instance?
column2:
database.schema.object.
The database part names another database on the same instance. For example, Sales.dbo.Orders addresses Orders in the Sales database.
Review source

column1: Which feature continuously replicates SQL Server data to Azure SQL Managed Instance for hybrid or migration use?
column2:
Managed Instance link.
The link keeps an instance-side copy synchronized using distributed availability groups. It is not a one-time export and import.
Review source

column1: Which Azure SQL deployment option lets you manage the guest operating system yourself?
column2:
SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines.
On a SQL Server Azure VM, you can configure the guest OS and install or manage SQL Server. With that control comes more maintenance work.
Review source

column1: Which extension adds Azure portal management and backup or patching automation for SQL Server on Azure Windows VMs?
column2:
The SQL IaaS Agent extension.
Register the Windows VM to expose SQL management options in Azure. The extension adds automation features but does not turn the VM into a fully managed database service.
Review source

column1: What workload does the transactional SQL database in Fabric serve, separate from its mirrored analytics copy?
column2:
Online transaction processing (OLTP).
It serves application transactions such as creating an order or updating inventory. Fabric analytics can read a separate mirrored copy of supported data.
Review source

column1: Where does SQL database in Fabric automatically mirror supported operational tables for analytics?
column2:
OneLake.
The service places supported mirrored data in OneLake. Analysts can use it without building a separate extraction pipeline or querying the live transactional tables.
Review source

column1: Which Fabric endpoint reads mirrored SQL database data without allowing updates to the mirrored rows?
column2:
The SQL analytics endpoint.
Use this endpoint to query mirrored data through T-SQL. You can create supported analytical objects such as views, but you cannot update the mirrored table rows there.
Review source

column1: Which tool supports .bacpac import/export and .dacpac deployment operations for SQL database in Fabric?
column2:
SqlPackage.
SqlPackage handles package operations for a supported Fabric SQL database. A BACPAC serves portability, while a DACPAC can deploy a database schema.
Review source

column1: Who manages built-in high availability for Azure SQL Database and Azure SQL Managed Instance?
column2:
Microsoft.
The platform runs the built-in availability infrastructure. You still design application retry behavior and choose any additional disaster recovery features you need.
Review source
